conventions.convention: Graded tensor maps use (f ⊗ g)(x ⊗ y) = (−1)^{|g||x|}f(x) ⊗ g(y); permutations use the corresponding Koszul signs.
Uncurved unsuspended A∞ operations have degree 2−n, begin at n=1, and satisfy the Stasheff sum with coefficient (−1)^{r+st}. No unit or graded commutativity is imposed.
For du=ab and dv=bc with |a|=p, the triple Massey expression is (−1)^{p+1}av+uc. The product includes all representative and null-homotopy choices and may be empty.
The reduced graded symmetric coalgebra uses symmetric coinvariants over a characteristic-zero field, positive symmetric lengths, and the unshuffle coproduct without factorial normalization.
The shifted space is W=V[1], with W^j=V^{j+1}; the symmetric Taylor operations q_n have degree +1 and no nullary operation.
Filtration completeness and separation are degreewise. Operations add positive input filtration indices; F^1W need not equal W. Maurer–Cartan inputs belong to F^1W^0.

Gauge paths satisfy C(w)=0 and w′=q_1^w(a), with a of shifted degree −1. Coefficients are polynomial in each filtration quotient without a common degree bound; gauge equivalence is generated by endpoint pairs. Right-placed forms encode a path as w−a dt.

Fixed-carrier deformations use coefficient completion of coaugmented tensor or symmetric direct-sum coalgebras, degreewise. Coderivations have zero nullary component; equivalences are continuous counital coaugmented degree-zero coalgebra automorphisms congruent to the identity modulo I.

load_bearing.statement: For the coefficient-complete carrier, each homogeneous endomorphism component is separated and complete for the order filtration, composition adds filtration orders, and coderivations form a closed graded Lie subalgebra. With dT=[D,T], g=F^1 l is a degreewise complete filtered differential graded Lie algebra.

For a filtered L∞ morphism and P=F^1W, the total-filtration-weight completion of the coaugmented symmetric coalgebra admits continuous structure and Taylor maps. For w∈P^0, Q(e^w)=c_q(w)e^w and F(e^w)=e^{f_*(w)}; the stated marked-input identity also holds.

For operations m_n of degree 2−n, b_n=(−1)^{n(n−1)/2}s_A m_n u_A^{⊗n} extend uniquely to a degree-one tensor coderivation B, and B²=0 is equivalent to the stated unsuspended A∞ identities. The corresponding degree-zero suspended morphism coefficients satisfy FB_A=B_DF exactly when the native A∞ morphism identities hold, including their composition signs.

For the coefficient-complete tensor or symmetric carrier, exponential and logarithm restrict to mutually inverse bijections between F^1 l^0 and all allowed identity-modulo-I coalgebra automorphisms, without finite-dimensionality or algebraic nilpotence of I.

For every initial Maurer–Cartan element w_* and every completed polynomial parameter a of shifted degree −1 in P=F^1W, there is a unique completed polynomial solution of w(0)=w_* and w′=q_1^w(a). Its curvature remains zero, and Picard iterations stabilize finitely in each quotient.

For the specified coefficient-complete deformation data and g=F^1 l with d=[D,−], R↦D+R bijects Maurer–Cartan elements with fixed-carrier codifferential deformations and identifies completed polynomial gauge classes with equivalence classes under all allowed coalgebra automorphisms. Variable-parameter gauge paths give exactly the orbit relation.

Every family of degree +1 graded-symmetric maps q_n:S^n(W)→W extends by the displayed finite unshuffle formula to the unique degree +1 coderivation of the reduced graded symmetric coalgebra with those corestrictions.

Filtered L∞ morphisms between complete filtered algebras over a characteristic-zero field have convergent Taylor pushforwards on F^1W^0 satisfying the stated curvature formula. They therefore preserve Maurer–Cartan elements continuously, and their pushforwards preserve composition and identities.

seams_checked.note: The supplier provides the cohomological unital DGA definition without graded commutativity. The consumer's strict A∞ construction, Massey closure calculation, and finite example use exactly its associative product, degree +1 square-zero differential, and signed Leibniz rule. Neither page attributes higher-algebra results to this reading prerequisite.

The actual item-level specialization uses the commutative unital real algebra, real-bilinear coefficient maps, finite coefficient sums, and fixed-unit normalization of def-formal-associative-deformation-of-a-commutative-algebra. The broader coderivation theorem proves its own correspondence and imports no differential-order, Poisson, existence, or formality assertion.

The BV page treats this as a convention and reading route and says its local proofs do not invoke higher Jacobi or deformation-classification results. It accurately retains characteristic zero, degreewise separated completeness, additive filtration bounds, and positive-filtration degree-zero input. For w=iS_h/h it explicitly distinguishes the required S_h∈h²A[[h]] from a general QME solution with constant or linear terms.
